review_notes: I read the whole file and compared it with Mathlib's AdicCompletion/Functoriality.lean. That file defines `pi` and `piEquivOfFintype` (which needs `Fintype`/`DecidableEq` on the index type) and says nothing about naturality in componentwise maps. `piEquivOfFG` here is not a competing version of `piEquivOfFintype`. It is built with `LinearEquiv.ofBijective (pi I M)`, so it reuses Mathlib's `pi` as its forward map. It also covers a different case: any index type, with `I` finitely generated. The file proves the two equivalences agree on finite products (`piEquivOfFG_eq_piEquivOfFintype`). The simp lemmas (`piEquivOfFG_apply`, `piEquivOfFG_of`, and so on) support the new equivalence and do not repeat existing API. I found no Mathlib `pi_comp_map` or `pi_map` lemma for `pi` and `map`, and a grep for `piMap`/`pi_map` in the AdicCompletion directory returned nothing. I did not review the imported helper declarations (`quotientPi`, `reduceModIdeal` from AdicModules.LinearAlgebra.Pi), because they are outside this file. I did not check whether they overlap with Mathlib's `Submodule.quotientPi`.
